# Hermes Agent: Onboarding & Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Welcome to Hermes Agent! This guide covers common setup steps, configuration patterns, architecture policies, and troubleshooting tips.

---

### 1. General & User Interface

**Q: Is Hermes CLI-only, or is there a Web UI?**  
Hermes includes a built-in web dashboard. Run:
```bash
hermes dashboard
```
This starts a local web server and opens the browser interface at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, which includes the embedded chat TUI.

**Q: How do I inspect skill usage and agent activity?**  
Skill metrics (`use_count`, `view_count`, timestamps) are stored in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`. You can view execution statistics via the CLI command `hermes insights` or in chat using `/insights`. For full LLM/tool tracing, enable the bundled Langfuse plugin: `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.

---

### 2. Model Configuration & Providers

**Q: Why are small local models (e.g., 4B–9B via Ollama) slow?**  
Hermes sends the full tool definition schema (~45 tools) on each API turn. Small models can struggle under large token prompts. To improve performance:
- Disable unnecessary toolsets via `hermes tools`.
- Set `terminal.backend: local` in `config.yaml` to remove container overhead.
- Use faster quantizations or scale to 32B+ parameter models for tool-heavy workflows.

**Q: Why does Hermes ignore my local `base_url` and try to reach Anthropic/OpenAI?**  
When `provider: auto` is set, Hermes scans your environment variables. If it finds keys like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, it routes there. To force your local endpoint:
```yaml
model:
  default: ollama/your-model
  provider: custom          # Use 'custom', not 'auto'
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
```

**Q: How do I configure Ollama Cloud, Azure Foundry, or Google Gemini?**
- **Ollama Cloud:** Use `provider: ollama-cloud` (routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`).
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Set `provider: azure-foundry` with `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`.
- **Google Gemini:** Set `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` via Google AI Studio. (Gemini CLI OAuth is unsupported).
- **Claude Pro/Max Subscriptions:** Anthropic API keys always bill as API usage. To use Pro/Max subscription allowances, authenticate via OAuth.

**Q: Does Hermes support smart/automatic cost routing between cheap and strong models?**  
No. Hermes has a strict design policy against per-turn complexity-based automatic model routing (`smart_model_routing`). Explicit model switching is supported via `/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`. Subagent models are defined explicitly via `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model`.

---

### 3. Messaging Platforms & Gateways

**Q: How do I set up Discord, Telegram, or other messaging platforms?**  
Run the interactive wizard:
```bash
hermes gateway setup
```
This guides you through tokens, allowed users, and channels without requiring manual edits to `.env` or `config.yaml`.

**Q: Why does Telegram reject me with "Unauthorized user"?**  
`allowed_chats` only filters group chats; it does **not** authorize DM users. To authorize users:
- **Option 1 (Allowlist):** In `config.yaml`, add:
  ```yaml
  telegram:
    allow_from: "YOUR_TELEGRAM_USER_ID"
  ```
- **Option 2 (Pairing):** DM your bot, get the pairing code, and approve it via CLI:
  ```bash
  hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>
  ```
- **Option 3:** Set `allow_all: true` under `telegram:`.

**Q: Can gateways send and receive files/images?**  
Yes. Platforms (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, Email, DingTalk) handle media:
- Uploaded text files and `.py` scripts are directly injected into prompt context.
- Tools and MCP plugins emit `MEDIA:<path>` tags, which the gateway converts into native platform file/image uploads or Markdown images.

**Q: Can I run multiple personas or profiles on one gateway?**  
Yes. Set `channel_prompts` in your platform config to bind distinct system prompts to specific channels. To run multiple isolated user profiles simultaneously, use gateway profile multiplexing.

---

### 4. Memory, Execution & Autonomy

**Q: What is the difference between `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, and `MEMORY.md`?**
- `SOUL.md`: Defines the agent’s personality, role, and system persona.
- `USER.md`: Stores information and preferences about the user (`target="user"` in memory tools).
- `MEMORY.md`: Stores general project and task context.
- *Note for local Honcho users:* Local backends (`http://localhost:8000`) do not require remote API keys.

**Q: What should I do when hitting the tool-call turn limit?**  
Hermes defaults to 90 turns per session (`agent.max_turns`). Override it per session with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`. For long-running autonomous workflows, use the persistent goal loop:
- Start: `/goal <your task>`
- Resume paused goals: `/goal resume`

---

### 5. OS & Deployment

- **Windows:** Native Windows 10/11 is supported via `install.ps1`. (WSL2 is only required if using the web dashboard's embedded terminal).
- **Docker / NAS:** Multi-arch images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon & Raspberry Pi). For NAS deployments (UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID) with bind-mount permission issues on `/opt/data`, supply `PUID=1000` and `PGID=10` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables.
- **Android / Termux:** Native support is available; installers automatically switch to the `termux-all` dependency profile.

---

### 6. Extending Hermes & Security

- **Custom Tools & Plugins:** Do not edit core files directly. Add custom tools by building a plugin in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and running `hermes plugins enable <plugin-name>`.
- **Memory Providers:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Implement the `MemoryProvider` interface in an external plugin.
- **Reporting Security Issues:** Report vulnerabilities privately to **security@nousresearch.com** or via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new). Do not open public issues.
